text:
anya: Heads-up — rough proposal for a 'load-sieve' quarantine to mitigate noisy tenants in shared GPU pools. Move offenders into a narrow, rate-limited slice that uses strict concurrency and fallback models so the rest of the pool keeps normal latency. PTAL.

ben: quick q — how do we detect 'noisy'? bursty spikes or sustained queueing?

anya: both. primary detection = p95 queue_time > 250ms AND tokens/sec > tenant_threshold. secondary signal = sustained KV-cache churn + GPU util spike. thresholds tuned per GPU profile.

carlos: interesting. what about low-rate but very expensive tenants (long context) — we can't just quarantine blindly.

anya: agreed. policy is graded: short violations -> light shaping (smaller batches, slight qps cap). repeated violations -> quarantine window (60s base + exponential backoff). in quarantine we cap concurrency to 1, reduce batch sizes and route to quantized fallback model.

jess: can you paste a config sketch?

anya: sure — here's a rough snippet:```yaml
policy:
  detection:
    queue_ms_p95: 250
    token_rate_per_min: 12000
  action:
    quarantine_duration_s: 60
    max_concurrency: 1
    batch_multiplier: 0.5
    fallback_model: "redwood/gpt-small-quant"
    grace_credits: 30  # seconds
```

infra-oncall: rollout plan? we need rollback criteria and alerts.

anya: plan: canary on pool-3 (us-west) for 24h. run synthetic noisy tenants + let 2 known noisy customers opt-in. monitor tail latency, throughput, fairness-index (Jain), unit-cost delta. auto-disable if any SLO breach or spillover fraction > 5%.

maya: please add a 'grace credit' bucket tied to reserved tenants so committed customers don't get quarantined for short bursts — store in redis with TTL.

ben: caching concern — quarantined tenants losing prefix cache could massively raise cost on rehydrate.

anya: we don't fully evict caches. keep shared read-only prefixes but disable prefetch and aggressive cache growth. that reduces memory churn while avoiding painful rehydrate storms.

sre-bot: deploy:load-sieve-policy -> pool-3 scheduled at 2025-06-10T15:12:30Z (dry-run mode) :robot_face:

carlos: test plan: client-replay scenarios at 0.8x,1.0x,1.5x noisy fraction; run for 6h windows; verify recovery and fairness metric.

jess: +1 to canary but need product sign-off for fallback model changes and customer-visible billing annotations.

maya: NIT: include quarantine events in billing/usage logs (meta tag) so customers can debug sudden latency changes. also include the reason code (QUEUE_P95, TOKEN_RATE).

ben: TL;DR: good pattern. deliverables before canary: final thresholds, runbook, rollback path, dashboards and billing annotation.

anya: I'll open an RFC doc + runbook and add perf dashboards this afternoon. will post link when ready. :thumbsup:

jess: thanks — if you need a quick review ping me.

anya: will do. thanks everyone.
